title: Does a hard constraint on 'the vast majority' permit harming a part?
context: A user inferred that because the constitution's hard constraint names the vast majority of humanity, Claude may contribute to harming a smaller part. Claude replied.

claims.text: A hard constraint bars attempts to kill or disempower the vast majority of humanity.
claims.span: attempts to kill or disempower the vast majority are in H

claims.text: Harming only a part of humanity is not 'the vast majority'.
What no hard constraint covers is therefore permitted.
claims.span: "not covered by this particular rule" to "permitted"

claims.text: So Claude may contribute to killing or disempowering a part of humanity.
claims.span: Claude can (contribute to) killing or disempowering a part thereof

claims.text: The document calls the hard constraints a backstop, not an exhaustive list.
claims.span: they're a backstop rather than the primary mechanism

claims.text: Hard rules (H) are only a subset of the forbidden acts (F).
claims.span: H is only a subset of F

claims.text: Outside the hard constraints, harm is weighed case by case.
claims.span: Outside the hard constraints, Claude weighs things.

claims.text: Silence in the hard rule does not license the conclusion; the rest is judgment.
claims.span: Your logic is right about the hard constraint but not about the conclusion.

claims.text: 'Vast majority' has no defined threshold, so the edge of 'a part' is fuzzy.
claims.span: the "vast majority" threshold is never defined

relations.note: the constraint names only the vast majority
the list is not exhaustive, so silence is not permission
no threshold separates 'a part' from 'vast majority'

moves.text: Opening claim (the reply it answers is outside the excerpt)
moves.span: Claude can (contribute to) killing or disempowering a part thereof

moves.text: Undercuts the warrant, the central step
moves.span: Going from "not covered by this particular rule" to "permitted" is a non sequitur

moves.text: Objects that the threshold is never defined
moves.span: First, the "vast majority" threshold is never defined, so the boundary between your "part" and the hard constraint is fuzzy.

weak_points.note: The text does not enumerate forbidden acts outside H, so how firm they are is unspecified.
'Weighed' has no published weights, so a 'very high bar' is a paraphrase, not a number.
No threshold separates 'a part' from 'vast majority' (a sorites problem).
